Legal notice

Fan project

Megamon is a game made by fans, free and non-profit. It has no ads or purchases.

It is not affiliated with, sponsored or endorsed by Nintendo, Creatures Inc., GAME FREAK or The Pokémon Company. Pokémon and all related names and characters are trademarks and property of their respective owners.

Cryptocurrencies

Megamon has no official cryptocurrency, token or NFT, and its author has not created any. Any token using the game's name was created by third parties: we take no responsibility for any purchase, sale or investment you make with them, and nothing here is investment advice.

Third-party content

Sprites from SpriteCollab (CC BY-NC 4.0, full credits in the repository's CREDITS.md). Pokédex data from PokeAPI. Pixelify Sans font (OFL). The music and sound effects are original to the project.

Contact and content removal

If you are a rights holder and want something removed, write to us and we'll take it down as soon as possible:

Source code:

Code license: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (you may use, study and modify it, but not to make money). Versions up to 14-10-2026 remain under MIT.

Privacy

If you create an account, we store your player name and your game (collection, coins, upgrades and stats) in Google Firebase so you can continue on any computer. If you sign in with Google, Firebase also stores your Google email to identify you (it is never shown to other players). We don't use your data for anything else, we don't share it, and there are no ads or tracking. As a guest, nothing is stored outside your browser.

Run history: your last 100 runs (your Pokémon, time, moves, and for recent runs how much damage each move did, which upgrades and level-up cards you took and how the run went) are kept with your game. Unless you turn off Share my run history in Settings, other players can see them on your profile, and we use shared runs to work out averages that help balance the game.

Friends and leaderboard: your nickname is public to other players. We store your friends list, whether you're online and your best times (with your nickname and your Pokémon).

Group games: your browser connects directly to your teammates' browsers (like a video call), so each of you may be able to see the others' IP address. Only play in a group with people you know. If a direct connection isn't possible, the game goes through Firebase's servers.

You can delete your account whenever you want (your nickname, friends and records are deleted too):
